speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you are a child with a low-grade fever, an itchy rash, and joint pain that started after taking antibiotics. To help me understand what is happening, did you have a strep throat or other infection before you started the medication?

speaker: Patient
text: 8-year-old girl. The patient was brought to the emergency department because of a 2-day history of low-grade fever, itchy rash, and generalized joint pain. The rash initially started in the antecubital and popliteal fossae before spreading to the trunk and distal extremities. One week ago, she was diagnosed with acute sinusitis and started on amoxicillin. She has no history of adverse drug reactions, and her immunizations are up to date.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Drug-induced hypersensitivity syndrome (DRESS) due to amoxicillin. The history of fever, rash, and arthralgia starting one week after amoxicillin initiation is classic for this reaction; I will order a complete blood count and liver function tests to confirm systemic involvement.
